task:
Three small fixes to The Bayes Group website (apps/bayes-group-site); change nothing else, and every existing acceptance test keeps passing except where this task changes that behavior.

1. Footer: remove the extra, unlabeled column of links (Services, Systems, Training, Engagements, About, Contact) at the right of the footer, on desktop and phones. The footer keeps exactly three groups: the wordmark with "AI enablement, training and custom development." and the email; the "Services" column (AI Enablement, Training, Custom Development, Systems engineering, Engagements); and the "Company" column (About, Contact); then the bottom line "© 2026 The Bayes Group". On desktop the three groups sit in one row (wordmark group wider, on the left); on phones they stack.

2. Contact page (/contact): give it the same navy page header band as the other inner pages (Services, Systems, Training, Engagements, About): navy background with the data-grid motif, the small uppercase teal eyebrow "CONTACT", the h1 "Book a consultation" in white, and under it the lead "Tell us what you're working on and we'll reply within one business day." and "Prefer email? hello@thebayesgroup.com" (the email stays a mailto link, readable on navy). The two-column form and "What happens next" card follow below on the page's normal background with the usual section spacing, unchanged otherwise.

3. Systems page (/systems) hero: on desktop the architecture diagram sits beside the heading and lead sentence (text in the left column, about 40% of the width; the diagram in the right column, vertically centered), instead of below them; on phones it stays below the text. Keep the diagram's content and labels exactly as they are.

review.feedback: No reviewer point was proven by a failing reproduction, so none blocks; they are listed above as open notes.
unproven: Footer still includes an extra column of links: the current Footer component nests a <nav aria-label="Footer"> containing two inner <nav class="footer-col"> elements, but the outer <nav> also has its own grid layout, effectively creating a fourth column with the Services/Systems/Training/Engagements/About/Contact links (the site-wide navigation). The tests require the extra unlabeled column to be removed; the current markup still renders those links, causing failures for R3‑R11.

Contact page header does not match the required navy band component used by other inner pages. The ContactPage currently includes its own <section class="page-hero band-navy"> with a DataGridMotif, but other pages use a shared band component with specific class names (e.g., .band-navy and .band-content). The current markup may not include the correct classes or structure for the eyebrow, lead, and email link styling, potentially breaking R12‑R20.

Systems page hero layout does not place the diagram beside the text on desktop. The SystemsPage (not shown) likely still nests the diagram after the text without a grid that switches at min-width:1024px, so R22‑R24 are not satisfied.
open_notes: Footer component (src/components/Footer.tsx) still includes the <nav aria-label="Footer" className="footer-nav"> which contains only the Services and Company columns – but there is no indication that the extra unlabeled column of all page links (Services, Systems, Training, Engagements, About, Contact) has been removed from the DOM. The current markup does not show any such column, but the task expects the footer to contain exactly three groups: the brand group (wordmark, text, email), a Services column with five specific links (AI Enablement, Training, Custom Development, Systems engineering, Engagements), and a Company column with About and Contact. The current SERVICE_LINKS array includes only the required five links but does not include the correct link labels (AI Enablement vs "AI Enablement" is correct) and order. However, the test likely expects the presence of a third column (the extra unlabeled column) to be absent. Since there is no fourth column present in the source, the issue may stem from CSS: the global.css does not define a 3‑track grid for the footer at desktop breakpoints, nor a stacked layout for phones. Without appropriate CSS, the footer groups may not be laid out as required (brand group wider on desktop, stacked on phones). The current CSS lacks any rules for .footer-inner or .footer-brand/.footer-nav grid layout, so the layout requirements R10 and R11 may not be satisfied. Add a CSS grid (e.g., .footer-inner { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 2fr 1fr 1fr; gap: 48px; } and modify with a media query for phones to stack) and ensure the three groups are correctly spaced and ordered. Also ensure the copyright line remains below a hairline after the grid.

Contact page (src/pages/ContactPage.tsx) does not contain the navy page header band with the data‑grid motif, eyebrow "CONTACT", h1 "Book a consultation", lead text, and mailto line as required by R12‑R20. The current ContactPage likely renders the form directly without that header band. Add a page‑header component (reuse the existing band used on other inner pages) with the required content and move the form section below it, preserving the existing IDs, labels and behavior.

Systems page hero layout (src/pages/SystemsPage.tsx) currently places the architecture diagram below the heading and lead sentence (as per the original design) and does not wrap the text and diagram in a grid that places them side‑by‑side on desktop. The task requires a two‑column grid with the text column (~40% width) left and the diagram (~60%) right, vertically centered, for screen widths >=1024px, and stacked for phones. Modify the SystemsPage to add the appropriate grid container and CSS (e.g., .systems-hero__grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0,2fr) minmax(0,3fr); align-items:center; } with a mobile fallback).

The Footer component still includes an extra Services column with links 'Systems', 'Engagements', 'About', 'Contact', which violates requirements R3-R9. The markup needs to be updated to remove this column and ensure only three groups (brand, Services, Company) are rendered, with correct links and ordering.
The Contact page header band is missing the data-grid motif SVG, violating requirement R13. The <DataGridMotif> component should be included within the band (as in other inner pages).

Footer still includes an extra column of links: the current Footer component nests a <nav aria-label="Footer"> containing two inner <nav class="footer-col"> elements, but the outer <nav> also has its own grid layout, effectively creating a fourth column with the Services/Systems/Training/Engagements/About/Contact links (the site-wide navigation). The tests require the extra unlabeled column to be removed; the current markup still renders those links, causing failures for R3‑R11.

Contact page header does not match the required navy band component used by other inner pages. The ContactPage currently includes its own <section class="page-hero band-navy"> with a DataGridMotif, but other pages use a shared band component with specific class names (e.g., .band-navy and .band-content). The current markup may not include the correct classes or structure for the eyebrow, lead, and email link styling, potentially breaking R12‑R20.

Systems page hero layout does not place the diagram beside the text on desktop. The SystemsPage (not shown) likely still nests the diagram after the text without a grid that switches at min-width:1024px, so R22‑R24 are not satisfied.

security.summary: The static marketing site remains functionally safe. No new code-level security issues were discovered in the recent layout changes. Existing concerns are limited to dependency CVEs in react‑router (medium) and missing HTTP security headers (medium). No injection, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, authentication, or data‑exposure problems are present.

findings.issue: react‑router‑dom 6.30.6 contains two known CVEs (information disclosure via client‑side constructor execution and open‑redirect via backslashes). The application only uses static internal routes, so the risk is low but the vulnerable version remains in the dependency tree.
findings.fix: Upgrade react‑router‑dom to a version where the CVEs are fixed (e.g., ^7.18.0) and update any API changes required by the newer major version.

ledger.issue: react‑router‑dom 6.30.6 contains two known CVEs (information disclosure via client‑side constructor execution and open‑redirect via backslashes). The application only uses static internal routes, so the risk is low but the vulnerable version remains in the dependency tree.
ledger.fix: Upgrade react‑router‑dom to a version where the CVEs are fixed (e.g., ^7.18.0) and update any API changes required by the newer major version.

ledger.issue: The static site does not emit essential HTTP security headers (Content‑Security‑Policy, X‑Frame‑Options, X‑Content‑Type‑Options, Referrer‑Policy, Strict‑Transport‑Security). Without them browsers may allow loading of unexpected resources or enable click‑jacking.
ledger.fix: Configure the hosting/web server or CDN to send appropriate security headers. Example values are already documented in DEPLOYMENT.md; ensure they are applied in production.

ui.summary: Phase 2 works through the fixed list of fixes taken when phase 1 finished; the other findings of that review are notes.

findings.issue: `.why-text` is applied to the Why The Bayes Group text column, but no CSS rule matches it. The spec requires the photo at 5 columns and the 2×2 points grid at 7 columns, with every text column beside a photo vertically centered. If this class was meant to carry the column placement or `align-self:center`, the column is falling back to default flow. It may sit top-aligned or span the wrong tracks on desktop.
findings.fix: Add the `.why-text` rule in global.css with the 7-column span, `align-self:center` and the 2×2 grid at ≥1024px. Alternatively, remove the class and use the existing grid or column class the other photo/text blocks use. Verify at 1280px that the points grid is centered against the photo.

findings.issue: The diagram renders an `arch-dark` class, but no stylesheet rule targets it. The dark variant is used in the navy Systems hero and the Home systems band. It must render `#102A4C` boxes, white box labels, `#5FC4C4` group labels and strokes, and `#1F8A8A` arrows. If any of those colors depend on `.arch-dark` descendant selectors, the dark variant silently falls back to light-variant fills or strokes on navy.
findings.fix: Either put the dark palette rules under `.arch-dark` in global.css, or drop the class if the colors are set as SVG attributes. Then check the navy Systems hero and Home band against the contrast table (#FFFFFF on #102A4C, #5FC4C4 on #102A4C, #1F8A8A on #0B1F3A).

findings.issue: `.examples` (the Example engagements section) has no CSS rule. The section needs the pale background, the 3-column card grid on desktop and the 14px muted note below the grid. If those come from other classes this is just a dead hook. If not, the section loses its pale band and the alternating white/pale rhythm the spec lists.
findings.fix: Confirm the pale background and the 3-column grid are applied by another class. Then either delete `examples` or give it the section rule (`background: var(--color-surface-teal)`, grid at ≥1024px).

findings.issue: The `home-page` wrapper class has no CSS. It is harmless on its own, but it adds to the unmatched-class noise and suggests a page-scoped rule was planned and never written.
findings.fix: Remove the class, or add the page-scoped rules it was meant to hold, so the unmatched-class audit reports zero.
